title: Brian Cashman reveals latest on Judge, Stanton injuries as Yankees eye trade deadline
content:
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. — As the New York Yankees try to jump-start their anemic offense, they will have to figure out how to win without the two pillars in the middle of their lineup. Neither appears to be nearing a return.

Aaron Judge will have his ribs re-examined during the All-Star break next week, but general manager Brian Cashman said the club is not anticipating the imaging to come back fully clean.

The Yankees are hopeful the images show that Judge, who was diagnosed last month with a stress fracture of the first rib on his right side, is healing. If so, Judge can start to add upper-body workouts to his rehab; he is currently limited in what he can do in the weight room, Cashman said.

“I don’t think we want to put him at risk of coming back while still injured,” Cashman said Thursday at Tropicana Field. “He should be asymptomatic before we turn him loose. If he’s asymptomatic and not feeling anything and they’re showing healing, it’s probably appropriate to get him going again. But we don’t want to — because the schedule is what it is — put him in the position where we’re putting him in jeopardy, where somehow it gets worse. Because the downside of that would be a real problem, in my opinion, from what I understand.

“The time frame that it would take to heal should allow him to be back with us this season.”

Cashman said he did not know whether Judge would be 100 percent when he returns. Those are answers that will come from the Yankees’ medical staff further along in his recovery.

Since the start of June, when Judge initially landed on the injured list, the Yankees entered Thursday 14-19 and tied for the fourth-worst offense in MLB by wRC+.

“Clearly, you miss him. That’s certainly part of it,” Cashman said of the Yankees’ ongoing struggles. “But, no, that’s not an answer to why we’re struggling with some consistently really good players that are going into collective slumps at the same time. That has nothing to do with Aaron Judge.”

The Yankees also continue to be without Giancarlo Stanton, who has not appeared in a game since April 24, when he strained his right calf. Manager Aaron Boone said last month that Stanton had a setback while rehabbing from the calf injury. Cashman said Thursday that it wasn’t a setback but rather a whole new injury.

Stanton was just cleared to start running after receiving platelet-rich plasma injections, but there’s no timeline for when he might return to the lineup.

“He had a new injury, so it kind of resets the whole thing,” Cashman said of Stanton.

“Ultimately, it was an unfortunate circumstance. Certainly we’d love to have him in that lineup, being the weapon that he is. But we have to let it heal. We have to give it the time it takes, and unfortunately, it takes time.”

As far as potential external upgrades, the trade deadline is still more than three weeks away. Cashman said he expects “heavier discussions” regarding possible trades after the MLB Draft, which is this weekend. Cashman would not directly say whether adding an impact bat is a priority at the trade deadline, given the uncertainty surrounding Judge and Stanton.

“I think we’re open-minded at the deadline to try to improve ourselves,” Cashman said. “Period. End of story. We’ll evaluate what’s available and try to push in on anything that makes sense that we can acquire that will make us better, whether it’s pitching or offense. So it doesn’t change anything.”
